description: rnews_main.rs:225 — stdin_bytes.len() is compared against MAX_BATCH_DECOMPRESSED_BYTES before calling parse_rnews_batch. For a compressed '#! gunbatch' batch the on-disk/on-wire compressed size can legitimately exceed 50 MiB (e.g. 1000 articles of near-1-MiB each, compressed to ~60% = ~600 MiB compressed). The check at line 225 rejects the batch before parse_rnews_batch even sees it, so the gunbatch decompressor — which enforces the real security cap via .take(limit+1) — is never reached. The correct pre-read bound for stdin should be MAX_BATCH_DECOMPRESSED_BYTES multiplied by some worst-case compression ratio (e.g. 2x), or the stdin check should be removed entirely and the protection left to decompress_gunbatch. As written, any compressed batch whose compressed size > 50 MiB is silently rejected even when its decompressed content is within the allowed 50 MiB.
title: SEC0: stdin size check rejects valid compressed gunbatch
